sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup by email; manager_id: listing direct reports for manager approval workflows; department: filtering employees by department; employment_status: filtering active/inactive/terminated employees

table leave_types | fields: id, leave_type_code, label, description, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type_code: unique lookup by code (e.g. 'annual', 'sick', 'emergency'); is_active: filtering active leave types for dropdowns and policy assignment

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type_id, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: leave_type_id -> leave_types.id | indexes: leave_type_id: joining policy to leave type for entitlement lookups; is_active: filtering active policies for balance calculations; policy_name: unique lookup by policy name

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: listing an employee's own leave requests; most frequent access pattern; status: filtering by status for manager approval queues and employee dashboards; leave_type_id: filtering requests by leave type; start_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; approved_by: manager viewing requests they approved or need to approve

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: looking up an employee's balance across all leave types; most frequent access pattern; policy_id: recalculating balances when a policy changes; fiscal_year: scoping balances to a specific fiscal year; employee_id, policy_id, fiscal_year: unique composite for balance enforcement — one balance row per employee per policy per year

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: looking up audit history for a specific entity (e.g. a leave request); performed_by: auditing actions by a specific user; action: filtering audit log by action type (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, APPROVE, REJECT); performed_at: time-range queries for audit reports

data_notes: Persistence design for the leave management module. Six conceptual tables defined: employees, leave_types, leave_policies, leave_requests, leave_balances, audit_logs. Six repository interfaces with concrete PostgreSQL implementations via pg Pool. All tables follow the domain model from DOMAIN.md and comply with GP-001 (repository pattern) and GP-002 (audit records via audit_logs). Index rationale reflects access patterns: employee-scoped lookups, status filtering for approval queues, date-range queries for calendar/overlap detection, and composite uniqueness for balance enforcement. The audit_logs table captures all state-changing operations (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, APPROVE, REJECT) as required by GP-002.
